baseline.scope: active core apps/packages/jobs workspaces; packages/platform excluded

rules: Existing findings are exact legacy debt: deletion is allowed, substitution or addition fails.
New @cuberoot/shared root imports are forbidden; use an explicit exported subpath.
Apps and jobs may not import another app's private source or public directory.
Build, test, artifact, subprocess and deploy edges require an explicit contract.

manualContracts.mechanism: CUBEOPT_ARTIFACT_DIR current pointer plus verified immutable bundle manifest
manualContracts.rationale: The large CubeOpt module, WASM and pruning table have an independent lifecycle and must not come from Web source or public assets.
manualContracts.replacement: Retain prepare, verify and atomic promote commands; deploy only the daemon code through the ordinary API workflow.

manualContracts.to: cubeopt Node child and WASM/table assets
manualContracts.mechanism: spawn built solve-daemon.mjs with the verified artifact-store environment
manualContracts.rationale: The child owns a large table and has independent lifecycle, queue and failure semantics.
manualContracts.replacement: Keep one production daemon manager and validate it through the bundled smoke entry; do not duplicate its stdio protocol.

manualContracts.mechanism: spawn with CUBE555_NATIVE_BIN, JAVA_BIN and CUBE555_HOME
manualContracts.rationale: The 5x5 solver is a separately installed native/Java runtime selected by environment.
manualContracts.replacement: Retain the explicit daemon adapter and deployment smoke; do not model it as a TypeScript import.

manualContracts.rationale: IP geolocation depends on a host executable and database outside the workspace.
manualContracts.replacement: Keep environment overrides and server tests; any replacement must preserve the same failure behavior.

manualContracts.to: packages/client icon generator and public icons
manualContracts.mechanism: dynamic import plus filesystem reads during Android asset generation
manualContracts.rationale: Android assets intentionally derive from the website brand source of truth.
manualContracts.replacement: If another consumer appears, extract a brand-assets build package; do not share runtime UI.

manualContracts.mechanism: pathToFileURL dynamic imports from the offline puzzle registry
manualContracts.rationale: The offline registry imports Web-private solver modules with mixed dependency closures; Clock is proven pure, while modules such as bicube and sia222 still include Web data-loading concerns.
manualContracts.replacement: PKG-02 candidate: extract one proven pure core at a time, splitting any Web loader before the module can join a runtime-neutral solver package.

manualContracts.to: repo stats/scramble and solver native analyzers/tables
manualContracts.mechanism: PowerShell orchestration plus JSON/binary artifact generation
manualContracts.rationale: The offline job consumes non-workspace solver binaries and publishes versioned static data outside core.
manualContracts.replacement: Keep the job boundary explicit; PS1-01 must map callers before any script relocation.

manualContracts.to: repo stats and deployed PostgreSQL derived tables
manualContracts.mechanism: JSON/TSV generation, workflow upload and database load
manualContracts.rationale: The daily job publishes static JSON and separately loads derived database tables.
manualContracts.replacement: Preserve builder, upload and load manifests as one reviewed contract; use the existing pipeline dry-run guard for changes.

manualContracts.to: repo stats/nemesizer and packages/server runtime loader
manualContracts.mechanism: workflow-generated binary files consumed through NEMESIZER_DATA_DIR
manualContracts.rationale: The producer writes compressed binary datasets outside core, while the API reads the deployed artifact directory at runtime.
manualContracts.replacement: Keep producer, workflow publication and server loader paths as one versioned artifact contract with parity fixtures.

evidence.contains: for dir in tools stats; do

manualContracts.mechanism: deterministic SQL generator writes a server migration
manualContracts.rationale: Curated algorithm import tooling intentionally produces backend schema/data migrations.
manualContracts.replacement: Keep the generated migration reviewed and committed; do not turn the generator into a server runtime dependency.

manualContracts.to: packages/server private utilities, routes, schema and migrations
manualContracts.mechanism: relative imports and direct fixture/source reads
manualContracts.rationale: Integration guards currently verify cross-layer behavior from the client test suite.
manualContracts.replacement: Move reusable contract fixtures to a neutral test boundary when the corresponding domain is refactored.

manualContracts.from: packages/server plus declared build and runtime inputs
manualContracts.mechanism: filtered workflow build and explicit server, daemon and migration artifacts
manualContracts.rationale: The API deploy must react to its real package inputs without being coupled to unrelated Web, Mobile or Mini Program changes.
manualContracts.replacement: Keep the workflow-path contract matrix aligned whenever a Server workspace dependency or deployment artifact changes.

evidence.contains: keeps the Core deploy boundary limited to real API production inputs

manualContracts.from: packages/client plus every workspace and deployment input consumed by the Next build
manualContracts.mechanism: GitHub Actions filtered build, packaged standalone output and remote restart
manualContracts.rationale: The Web app already has an independently built and deployed runtime artifact.
manualContracts.replacement: Keep this deployment independent; a future physical directory move must update the trigger and sparse checkout atomically.

evidence.contains: keeps the Next deploy boundary aligned with its build and runtime inputs
